units.zh: 南齊書卷二十一‧列傳第二
units.en: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 21 — Biographies 2
units.literal: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 21 — Biographies 2

units.zh: 文惠太子
units.en: Crown Prince Wenhui
units.literal: Crown Prince Wenhui

units.zh: 文惠太子長懋字雲喬，世祖長子也。
units.en: Crown Prince Wenhui, Xiao Zhangmao, courtesy name Yunqiao, was the eldest son of Emperor Wu.
units.literal: Crown Prince Wenhui Zhangmao, courtesy name Yunqiao, was the eldest son of Emperor Wu.

units.zh: 世祖年未弱冠而生太子，爲太祖所愛。
units.en: Emperor Wu was not yet twenty when Xiao Zhangmao was born, and Xiao Daocheng, the Grand Ancestor, doted on him.
units.literal: Emperor Wu had not yet come of age when the crown prince was born, and the Grand Ancestor loved him.

units.zh: 姿容豐潤，小字白澤。
units.en: He was handsome and well favored; in childhood he was called Baize.
units.literal: His bearing was full and fair; his childhood name was Baize.

units.zh: 宋元徽末，隨世祖在郢。
units.en: Late in the Yuánhuī era of Song he was with Emperor Wu at Ying.
units.literal: At the end of the Yuánhuī era of Song, he followed Emperor Wu at Ying.

units.zh: 世祖還鎮盆城拒沈攸之，使太子勞接將帥，親侍軍旅。
units.en: When Emperor Wu went back to hold Pencheng against Shen Youzhi, he sent the prince to receive the commanders and share the hardships of the camp.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu returned to garrison at Pencheng to resist Shen Youzhi, he had the crown prince greet the generals and take part in the army in person.

units.zh: 除秘書郎，不拜。
units.en: He was named secretary gentleman but declined to take up the post.
units.literal: He was appointed secretary gentleman but did not accept the office.

units.zh: 授輔國將軍，遷晉熙王撫軍主簿。
units.en: He was made General Who Assists the State and moved to be chief clerk on Prince Jinxi's pacifying staff.
units.literal: He was made General Who Assists the State and transferred to serve as steward to the General Who Pacifies the Army under Prince Jinxi.

units.zh: 事寧，世祖遣太子還都。
units.en: After peace was restored, Emperor Wu sent the prince back to the capital.
units.literal: When the affair was settled, Emperor Wu sent the crown prince back to the capital.

units.zh: 太祖方創霸業，心存嫡嗣，謂太子曰：「汝還，吾事辦矣。」
units.en: Xiao Daocheng was then laying the foundations of rule and had the succession at heart. He told the prince, "When you return, my work is finished."
units.literal: The Grand Ancestor was then founding his hegemony and kept the legitimate heir in mind. He told the crown prince: "When you return, my task is done."

units.zh: 處之府東齋，令通文武賓客。
units.en: He quartered him in the east study of the princely residence and opened the doors to guests civil and martial alike.
units.literal: He lodged him in the east study of the princely residence and allowed him access to civil and military guests.

units.zh: 敕荀伯玉曰：「我出行日，城中軍悉受長懋節度。
units.en: He instructed Xun Boyu, "On days when I leave the city, every soldier in the capital shall answer to Zhangmao.
units.literal: He charged Xun Boyu: "On days when I go out, all troops in the city shall obey Zhangmao's command.

units.zh: 我雖不行，內外直防及諸門甲兵，悉令長懋時時履行。」
units.en: Even when I stay in, let Zhangmao walk the inner and outer watches and the armored guards at every gate."
units.literal: Even when I do not go out, let Zhangmao from time to time inspect all inner and outer guards and the armored men at every gate."

units.zh: 轉秘書丞，以與宣帝諱同，不就，改除中書郎，遷黃門侍郎，未拜。
units.en: He was transferred to secretary director, but the title matched the taboo of Emperor Xuan of Jin, so he declined; he was reassigned gentleman of the palace secretariat and promoted gentleman attendant at the yellow gate, without yet taking office.
units.literal: He was transferred to secretary director, but since that title matched the taboo name of Emperor Xuan of Jin, he did not take it; he was reassigned as gentleman of the palace secretariat and promoted to gentleman attendant at the yellow gate, but had not yet assumed office.

units.zh: 升明三年，太祖將受禪，世祖已還京師，以襄陽兵馬重鎮，不欲處他族，出太子爲持節、都督雍梁二州、郢州之竟陵、司州之隨郡軍事、左中郎將、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。
units.en: In Shengming year 3, as Xiao Daocheng prepared to accept the throne, Emperor Wu was already in the capital. Xiangyang held the empire's horses and arms, and he would not trust another house with it—so he sent the prince out as bearer of the staff, superintendent of Yong and Liang, of Jingling in Ying and Sui in Si, left central commander, colonel pacifying the barbarians, and inspector of Yong.
units.literal: In the third year of Shengming, as the Grand Ancestor was about to receive the abdication, Emperor Wu had already returned to the capital. Because Xiangyang was a key stronghold for troops and horses and he did not wish to place another clan in charge, he sent out the crown prince as bearer of the staff, superintendent of military affairs in the two provinces of Yong and Liang, Jingling in Ying province, and Sui commandery in Si province, left central commander, colonel pacifying the barbarians, and inspector of Yong province.

units.zh: 建元元年，封南郡王，邑二千戶。
units.en: In the first year of Jianyuan he was enfeoffed Prince of Nan commandery, fief of two thousand households.
units.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nan commandery, with a fief of two thousand households.

units.zh: 江左未有嫡皇孫封王，始自此也。
units.en: South of the Yangtze no legitimate imperial grandson had ever been made a prince before; the precedent began here.
units.literal: Never before in the lands south of the Yangtze had a legitimate imperial grandson been enfeoffed as prince; it began with this.

units.zh: 進號征虜將軍。
units.en: His title was raised to General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
units.literal: He was advanced in title to General Who Subdues the Barbarians.

units.zh: 先是，梁州刺史范柏年誘降晉壽亡命李烏奴，討平氐賊楊城、蘇道熾等，頗著威名。
units.en: Earlier Fan Bonian, inspector of Liang, had won over Li Wunu, a Jinshou outlaw, and put down the Di chiefs Yang Cheng and Su Daoshi, until his name carried weight.
units.literal: Earlier, Fan Bonian, inspector of Liang province, had induced the fugitive Li Wunu of Jinshou to surrender and had crushed the Di bandits Yang Cheng, Su Daoshi, and others, winning considerable renown.

units.zh: 沈攸之事起，柏年遣將陰廣宗領軍出魏興聲援京師，而候望形勢。
units.en: When Shen Youzhi rose, Bonian sent Yin Guangzong out of Weixing with an army, ostensibly to aid the capital while he read the wind.
units.literal: When Shen Youzhi's rebellion arose, Bonian sent his general Yin Guangzong to lead troops out from Weixing to signal support for the capital while watching how events unfolded.

units.zh: 事平，朝廷遣王玄邈代之。
units.en: Once the revolt was crushed, the court sent Wang Xuanmiao to relieve him.
units.literal: When the affair was pacified, the court sent Wang Xuanmiao to replace him.

units.zh: 烏奴勸柏年據漢中不受命，柏年計未決，玄邈已至，柏年遲回魏興不肯下。
units.en: Li Wunu urged Bonian to seize Hanzhong and defy the summons. Bonian wavered; Xuanmiao was already on the road, yet Bonian hung back at Weixing and would not descend.
units.literal: Li Wunu urged Bonian to hold Hanzhong and refuse the order; Bonian had not yet decided when Xuanmiao arrived. Bonian lingered at Weixing and would not come down.

units.zh: 太子慮其爲變，乃遣說柏年，許啓爲府長史，柏年乃進襄陽，因執誅之。
units.en: The prince, fearing a mutiny, sent envoys promising to name Bonian chief steward of his staff if he came in. Bonian marched to Xiangyang—and was seized and put to death.
units.literal: The crown prince, fearing he might rebel, sent someone to persuade Bonian, promising to recommend him as chief steward of the princely establishment. Bonian then advanced to Xiangyang, where he was seized and executed.

units.zh: 柏年，梓潼人，徙居華陽，世爲土豪，知名州里。
units.en: Bonian came from Zitong and had settled in Huayang; for generations his clan had been great landlords, famed in the province.
units.literal: Bonian was a native of Zitong who had moved to live at Huayang; for generations his family had been local magnates, known throughout the province.

units.zh: 宋泰始中，氐寇斷晉壽道，柏年以倉部郎假節領數百人慰勞通路，自益州道報命。
units.en: In Song's Taishi era Di raiders severed the Jinshou road. Bonian, then gentleman of the grain bureaus, took the staff and led several hundred men to reopen the route and hearten the garrisons, then returned by the Yizhou road to report.
units.literal: In the Taishi era of Song, Di raiders cut the road to Jinshou. Bonian, as gentleman of the bureaus of grain, took the staff of authority and led several hundred men to comfort troops and reopen the route, returning by way of Yizhou to report.

units.zh: 除晉壽太守。
units.en: He was made administrator of Jinshou.
units.literal: He was appointed administrator of Jinshou.

units.zh: 討平氐賊，遂爲梁州。
units.en: When the Di were pacified he became inspector of Liang.
units.literal: After he had put down the Di bandits, he became inspector of Liang province.

units.zh: 柏年強立，善言事，以應對爲宋明帝所知。
units.en: Bonian was imposing in person and quick in counsel; Emperor Ming of Song prized his repartee.
units.literal: Bonian was forceful in bearing and skilled in speech; his ready replies won him notice from Emperor Ming of Song.

units.zh: 旣被誅，巴西太守柳弘稱啓太祖，敕答曰：「柏年幸可不爾，爲之恨恨！」
units.en: After the execution Liu Hong of Baxi memorialized Xiao Daocheng. The reply read, "Bonian might have been spared this—I grieve for it!"
units.literal: After he was executed, Liu Hong, administrator of Baxi, submitted a memorial to the Grand Ancestor. The edict in reply read: "It would have been fortunate if Bonian had not come to this; I deeply regret it!"

units.zh: 時襄陽有盜發古塚者，相傳云是楚王塚，大獲寶物玉屐、玉屏風、竹簡書、青絲編。
units.en: About then robbers broke into an old tomb at Xiangyang said to be a King of Chu's. They carried off jade sandals, a jade screen, bamboo slips, and green-silk bindings in great quantity.
units.literal: About that time grave robbers opened an ancient tomb at Xiangyang; tradition held it was the tomb of a King of Chu. They took a great haul of treasures: jade sandals, a jade screen, bamboo slips bound with green silk cord.

units.zh: 簡廣數分，長二尺，皮節如新。
units.en: The slips were several inches across and two feet long; the bamboo skin looked newly cut.
units.literal: The slips were several inches wide and two feet long; the outer bark joints seemed fresh.

units.zh: 盜以把火自照，後人有得十餘簡，以示撫軍王僧虔，僧虔云是科斗書《考工記》，《周官》所闕文也。
units.en: The thieves lit torches to read by. Later a man came by a dozen-odd slips and showed them to Wang Sengqian, general who pacifies the army. Sengqian said they were tadpole script, the Artificers' Record—the portion the Offices of Zhou lacks.
units.literal: The robbers held torches to see by. Later someone obtained more than ten slips and showed them to the General Who Pacifies the Army Wang Sengqian; Sengqian said they were tadpole-script "Artificers' Record," text missing from the Offices of Zhou.

units.zh: 是時州遣按驗，頗得遺物，故有同異之論。
units.en: The province sent investigators and recovered part of the hoard, which is why accounts differ.
units.literal: At that time the province sent men to investigate and recovered many of the relics, hence conflicting accounts.

units.zh: 會北虜南侵，上慮當出樊、沔。
units.en: When the northern enemy pushed south, the throne feared it might have to withdraw toward Fan and Mian.
units.literal: When the northern barbarians invaded south, the emperor feared the court might have to move out toward Fan and Mian.

units.zh: 二年，征爲侍中、中軍將軍，置府，鎮石頭。
units.en: In year 2 he was recalled as palace attendant and general of the central army, given a staff, and posted to Stone City.
units.literal: In year 2 he was summoned as palace attendant and general of the central army, with a staff established, and garrisoned at Stone City.

units.zh: 穆妃薨，成服日，車駕出臨喪，朝議疑太子應出門迎。
units.en: When Consort Mu died, on the day he finished putting on mourning the emperor rode out in person. The court debated whether the prince should go out to meet the carriage.
units.literal: When Consort Mu died, on the day of completing mourning dress the imperial carriage went out to condole. Court discussion was divided on whether the crown prince should go out to welcome it.

units.zh: 左僕射王儉曰：「尋《禮記‧服問》『君所主夫人妻、太子、嫡婦』，言國君爲此三人爲主喪也。
units.en: Wang Jian, left vice minister, said, "The Book of Rites, 'Dress Questions,' says the lord himself presides for his wife, the heir apparent's wife, and the chief daughter-in-law—that is, the sovereign leads mourning for these three.
units.literal: Left vice minister Wang Jian said: "If we look to 'Dress Questions' in the Book of Rites—'for the lord's wife, the heir apparent's wife, and the chief daughter-in-law, the lord himself presides over mourning'—that means the sovereign presides over mourning for these three.

units.zh: 今鸞輿臨降，自以主喪而至，雖因事撫慰，義不在吊，南郡以下不應出門奉迎。
units.en: Today the imperial carriage comes down as chief mourner. Comfort may be offered on the way, but the visit is not a condolence call; the Prince of Nan and his household should not go out to welcome it.
units.literal: Now the imperial phoenix carriage descends; it comes in its capacity as chief mourner. Though there is incidental consolation, the rite is not one of condolence; the Prince of Nan commandery and those below him should not go out to welcome it.

units.zh: 但尊極所臨，禮有變革，權去杖絰，移立戶外，足表情敬，無煩止哭。
units.en: Yet when the supreme presence arrives, ritual bends: lay aside staff and sackcloth for the moment and stand outside the door—reverence enough without forcing an end to weeping.
units.literal: Yet where the supreme honor arrives, ritual may bend: for the moment put aside staff and hemp, and stand outside the door—enough to show reverence without requiring one to cease weeping.

units.zh: 皇太子旣一宮之主，自應以車駕幸宮，依常奉候。
units.en: The heir apparent is master of his own palace; when the carriage honors his quarters he should receive it in the usual way.
units.literal: The heir apparent, as master of his palace, should in any case receive the imperial carriage when it visits his quarters in the usual form of attendance.

units.zh: 旣當成服之日，吉凶不容相干，宜以衰幘行事。
units.en: On the day mourning dress is completed, joy and grief must not mingle—he should go in hemp cap and headband.
units.literal: On a day when mourning dress is completed, auspicious and inauspicious rites must not clash; he should act wearing hemp cap and headband.

units.zh: 望拜止哭，率由舊章。
units.en: Cease weeping to bow toward the carriage—that follows old precedent.
units.literal: Stopping tears to perform the bow toward the carriage—all according to established precedent.

units.zh: 尊駕不以臨吊，奉迎則惟常體，求之情禮，如爲可安。」
units.en: The supreme carriage does not come to mourn; to meet it is only ordinary courtesy. Judged by feeling and rite, that should suffice."
units.literal: Since the supreme carriage does not come for condolence, welcoming it is only the ordinary courtesy. Weighing feeling and rite, that seems acceptable."

units.zh: 解侍中。
units.en: He was relieved of palace attendant.
units.literal: He was relieved of palace attendant.

units.zh: 上以太子哀疾，不宜居石頭山障，移鎮西州。
units.en: The emperor, finding the prince in grief and poor health, thought Stone City's mountain redoubts unsuitable and shifted him to West Province.
units.literal: The emperor, because the crown prince was in mourning and ill, thought Stone City's mountain defenses unsuitable and moved him to garrison West Province.

units.zh: 四年，遷使持節、都督南徐兗二州諸軍事、征北將軍、南徐州刺史。
units.en: In year 4 he was transferred bearer of the staff, superintendent of southern Xu and Yan, general who campaigns north, and inspector of southern Xu.
units.literal: In year 4 he was transferred as bearer of the staff of authority, superintendent of military affairs in the two provinces of southern Xu and Yan, general who campaigns north, and inspector of southern Xu province.

units.zh: 世祖即位，爲皇太子。
units.en: When Emperor Wu acceded, Xiao Zhangmao was made crown prince.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he was made crown prince.

units.zh: 初，太祖好《左氏春秋》，太子承旨諷誦，以爲口實。
units.en: In his youth Xiao Daocheng loved the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals; the prince recited it at his bidding until the text lived on his tongue.
units.literal: At first the Grand Ancestor loved the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals; the crown prince carried out his intent by reciting it until it became a favorite topic.

units.zh: 旣正位東儲，善立名尚，禮接文士，畜養武人，皆親近左右，布在省闥。
units.en: Once he held the eastern palace he courted a fine name, welcomed men of letters, and kept fighting men near—all of them in his inner circle, stationed through the palace offices.
units.literal: Once installed as heir apparent, he cultivated reputation and esteem, received scholars with courtesy, and kept martial men about him—all close at hand, placed throughout the palace offices.

units.zh: 永明三年，於崇正殿講《孝經》，少傅王儉以擿句令太子僕周顒撰爲義疏。
units.en: In Yongming year 3 he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety in the Hall of Correct Reverence; Junior Tutor Wang Jian picked out passages and had Palace Adjutant Zhou Yong draft a commentary.
units.literal: In the third year of Yongming, he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety in the Hall of Correct Reverence; Junior Tutor Wang Jian, by selecting passages, had Palace Adjutant Zhou Yong compile a commentary.

units.zh: 五年冬，太子臨國學，親臨策試諸生，於坐問少傅王儉曰：「《曲禮》云『無不敬』。
units.en: That winter in the fifth year the crown prince went to the National Academy, sat in person to examine the students, and asked Junior Tutor Wang Jian from his seat: "The Qu Li says, 'There is nothing to which one is not reverent.'
units.literal: In the winter of the fifth year the crown prince attended the National Academy, personally presided over the written examination of the students, and from his seat asked Junior Tutor Wang Jian: "The Qu Li chapter of the Record of Rites says, 'There is nothing to which one is not reverent.'

units.zh: 尋下之奉上，可以盡禮，上之接下，慈而非敬。
units.en: From below to above one may exhaust every rite; from above to those below there is kindness, not reverence.
units.literal: Serving from below upward can exhaust ritual; receiving those below from above is kindness, not reverence.

units.zh: 今總同敬名，將不爲昧？」
units.en: To call both by the single name 'reverence'—will that not blur what is distinct?"
units.literal: To use the same name 'reverence' for both—will that not obscure the distinction?"

units.zh: 儉曰：「鄭玄云『禮主於敬』，便當是尊卑所同。」
units.en: Wang Jian replied: "Zheng Xuan says 'Ritual takes reverence as its foundation'—then high and low should share it alike."
units.literal: Wang Jian said: "Zheng Xuan says 'Ritual takes reverence as its foundation'—that should hold for superior and inferior alike."

units.zh: 太子曰：「若如來通，則忠惠可以一名，孝慈不須另稱。」
units.en: The crown prince said: "If that holds all the way through, loyalty and kindness could be one name, and filial piety and compassion would need no second term."
units.literal: The crown prince said: "If one follows that through, loyalty and generosity could share one name, and filial piety and compassion would need no separate terms."

units.zh: 儉曰：「尊卑號稱，不可悉同，愛敬之名，有時相次。
units.en: Wang Jian said: "Titles for high and low cannot all match; the names love and reverence sometimes come one after the other.
units.literal: Wang Jian said: "Titles for superior and inferior cannot all be identical; the names love and reverence sometimes follow in sequence.

units.zh: 忠惠之異，誠以聖旨，孝慈互舉，竊有徵據。
units.en: Loyalty and kindness differ by the sage's meaning; filial piety and compassion are set side by side—I have warrant for that.
units.literal: The difference between loyalty and generosity truly rests on the sage's intent; filial piety and compassion are raised in turn—I have private evidence for this.

units.zh: 《禮》云『不勝喪比於不慈不孝』，此則其義。」
units.en: The Record of Rites says, 'One who cannot bear mourning is like one unkind and unfilial'—that is the proof."
units.literal: The Record of Rites says 'One who cannot bear mourning is like one who is unkind and unfilial'—that is the point."

units.zh: 太子曰：「資敬奉君，資愛事親，兼此二塗，唯在一極。
units.en: The crown prince said: "Reverence feeds service to the ruler, love feeds service to parents—both roads meet at one pole.
units.literal: The crown prince said: "Drawing on reverence to serve the ruler and on love to serve one's parents—both paths share a single pole.

units.zh: 今乃移敬接下。
units.en: Yet now reverence is moved down to those below.
units.literal: Yet now reverence is shifted to receiving those below.

units.zh: 豈復在三之義？」
units.en: How does that still fit the meaning of 'three'?"
units.literal: How can that still accord with the sense of 'three'?"

units.zh: 儉曰：「資敬奉君，必同至極，移敬逮下，不慢而已。」
units.en: Wang Jian said: "Reverence in serving the ruler must reach the same pole; carrying reverence down to those below means only not to slight them."
units.literal: Wang Jian said: "Drawing on reverence to serve the ruler must reach the same pole; extending reverence to those below means only not to be disrespectful."

units.zh: 太子曰：「敬名雖同，深淺旣異，而文無差別，彌復增疑。」
units.en: The crown prince said: "The name is one, but depth and shallowness differ—and the wording shows no gap, which only adds doubt."
units.literal: The crown prince said: "Though the name is the same, the depth and shallowness clearly differ—yet the text makes no distinction, which only deepens the doubt."

units.zh: 儉曰：「繁文不可備設，略言深淺已見。
units.en: Wang Jian said: "Full phrasing cannot all be laid out; in brief, depth and shallowness are already clear.
units.literal: Wang Jian said: "Elaborate wording cannot all be set forth; stated briefly, the depth and shallowness are already plain.

units.zh: 《傳》云『不忘恭敬，民之主也』。
units.en: The Commentary says, 'Never forget reverence and respect—such a one is lord of the people.'
units.literal: The Commentary says 'Never forget reverence and respect—such a one is lord of the people.'

units.zh: 《書》云『奉先思孝，接下思恭』。
units.en: The Documents say, 'In serving the ancestors, think of filial piety; in receiving those below, think of respect.'
units.literal: The Documents say 'In serving the ancestors, think of filial piety; in receiving those below, think of respect.'

units.zh: 此又經典明文，互相起發。」
units.en: Here again the classics speak plainly, each line drawing the other out."
units.literal: Here again is explicit scripture, each passage calling forth the other."

units.zh: 太子問金紫光祿大夫張緒，緒曰：「愚謂恭敬是立身之本，尊卑所以竝同。」
units.en: The crown prince asked Zhang Xu, minister of the palace with the golden seal and purple cord. Zhang said: "I take reverence and respect as the root of standing in the world—that is why high and low share them."
units.literal: The crown prince asked Zhang Xu, Minister of the Palace with the Golden Seal and Purple Cord. Zhang said: "I hold that reverence and respect are the root of taking one's stand in the world—hence superior and inferior share them alike."

units.zh: 太子曰：「敬雖立身之本，要非接下之稱。
units.en: The crown prince said: "Reverence may be the root of the person, but it is not the name for receiving those below.
units.literal: The crown prince said: "Though reverence is the root of self-cultivation, it is hardly the term for receiving those below.

units.zh: 《尚書》云『惠鮮鰥寡』，何不言恭敬鰥寡邪？」
units.en: The Documents say, 'Be kind to widowers and widows'—why not say, 'be reverent and respectful to widowers and widows'?"
units.literal: The Documents say 'Be kind to widowers and widows'—why not say 'be reverent and respectful to widowers and widows'?"

units.zh: 緒曰：「今別言之，居然有恭惠之殊，總開記首，所以共同斯稱。」
units.en: Zhang said: "Spoken apart, respect and kindness plainly differ; at the head of a record they are opened together, and so share one name."
units.literal: Zhang said: "When spoken of separately, the difference between respect and kindness is plain; at the opening of a record they are taken together, and therefore share one designation."

units.zh: 竟陵王子良曰：「禮者敬而已矣。
units.en: The prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, said: "Ritual is reverence, nothing beyond it.
units.literal: The prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, said: "Ritual is reverence and nothing more.

units.zh: 自上及下，愚謂非嫌。」
units.en: From top to bottom—I see no problem in that."
units.literal: From highest to lowest—I see no difficulty."

units.zh: 太子曰：「本不謂有嫌，正欲使言與事符，輕重有別耳。」
units.en: The crown prince said: "I never called it a problem—I only want speech to fit the deed, with light and heavy kept apart."
units.literal: The crown prince said: "I never said there was difficulty—I only want words to match affairs, with lighter and heavier clearly distinguished."

units.zh: 臨川王映曰：「先舉必敬，以明大體，尊卑事數，備列後章，亦當不以總略而礙。」
units.en: The prince of Linchuan, Xiao Ying, said: "To open with reverence is to show the great pattern; the counts of rank and rite are spelled out in later chapters—a summary should not stand in the way."
units.literal: The prince of Linchuan, Xiao Ying, said: "To lead with reverence is to clarify the larger frame; the details of rank and ritual are fully set out in later chapters—one should not let a general summary block that."

units.zh: 太子又以此義問諸學生，謝幾卿等十一人，竝以筆對。
units.en: The crown prince put the same question to the students; Xie Jiqing and eleven others all answered in writing.
units.literal: The crown prince again put this question to the students; Xie Jiqing and eleven others all answered in writing.

units.zh: 太子問王儉曰：「《周易乾卦》本施天位，而《說卦》云『帝出乎《震》』。
units.en: The crown prince asked Wang Jian: "The Qian hexagram of the Book of Changes is set for Heaven's place, yet the Explanation of the Trigrams says, 'The Lord emerges from Zhen.'
units.literal: The crown prince asked Wang Jian: "The Qian hexagram of the Book of Changes originally applies to Heaven's position, yet the Explanation of the Trigrams says 'The Lord emerges from Zhen.'

units.zh: 《震》本非天，義豈相主？」
units.en: Zhen is not Heaven by nature—how can one meaning rule the other?"
units.literal: Zhen is not Heaven by nature—how can the meanings preside over each other?"

units.zh: 儉曰：「《乾》健《震》動，天以運動爲德，故言『帝出《震》』。」
units.en: Wang Jian said: "Qian is firm, Zhen is movement; Heaven's virtue is movement, hence 'the Lord emerges from Zhen.'"
units.literal: Wang Jian said: "Qian is strength, Zhen is motion; Heaven takes motion as its virtue, hence 'the Lord emerges from Zhen.'"

units.zh: 太子曰：「天以運動爲德，君自體天居位，《震》雷爲象，豈體天所出？」
units.en: The crown prince said: "If Heaven's virtue is movement, the ruler bodies forth Heaven in his seat—yet Zhen, Thunder, is the image. How is that the bodying-forth of Heaven?"
units.literal: The crown prince said: "If Heaven takes motion as its virtue, the ruler himself embodies Heaven in his station—yet Zhen, Thunder, is the image. How can that be what embodies Heaven's emergence?"

units.zh: 儉曰：「主器者莫若長子，故受之以《震》。
units.en: Wang Jian said: "He who holds the vessel—none like the eldest son—so he receives Zhen.
units.literal: Wang Jian said: "He who holds the vessel is none so fit as the eldest son—hence he receives Zhen.

units.zh: 萬物出乎《震》，故亦帝所與焉。」
units.en: The ten thousand things come from Zhen—so the Lord's share is there too."
units.literal: All things emerge from Zhen—thus the Lord's portion lies there as well."

units.zh: 儉又諮太子曰：「《孝經》『仲尼居，曾子侍』。
units.en: Wang Jian went on to ask the crown prince: "In the Classic of Filial Piety, 'Confucius was at rest and Zengzi attended.'
units.literal: Wang Jian further addressed the crown prince: "In the Classic of Filial Piety, 'Confucius was at rest and Zengzi attended him.'

units.zh: 夫孝理弘深，大賢方盡其致，何故不授顏子，而寄曾生？」
units.en: Filial piety runs wide and deep; only a great sage can reach its limit. Why not give it to Yan Hui, but lodge it with Master Zeng?"
units.literal: The principle of filial piety is vast and deep; only a great sage can exhaust its reach. Why was it not given to Yan Hui but entrusted to Master Zeng?"

units.zh: 太子曰：「曾生雖德慚體二，而色養盡禮，去物尚近，接引非隔，弘宣規教，義在於此。」
units.en: The crown prince said: "Master Zeng's virtue did not match the Sage in body, yet he nourished his parents' looks to the full of ritual; he was still close to things, with no break in the line—to spread the teaching's rule, the reason is here."
units.literal: The crown prince said: "Though Master Zeng's virtue fell short of matching the Sage in stature, his nourishing his parents' countenance fulfilled the rites in full; he was still near to things, without a gap in transmission—to spread and proclaim the regulations of the teaching, the point lies here."

units.zh: 儉曰：「接引非隔，弘宣雖易，去聖轉遠，其事彌輕。
units.en: Wang Jian said: "No break in the line, and spreading the teaching is easy—but the farther from the Sage, the lighter the thing grows.
units.literal: Wang Jian said: "Without a gap in transmission, spreading the teaching is easy—but the farther one stands from the Sage, the lighter the matter becomes.

units.zh: 旣云『人能弘道』，將恐人輕道廢。」
units.en: It is said, 'Man can enlarge the Way'—I fear men will slight the Way and let it die."
units.literal: Since it is said 'it is man who enlarges the Way,' I fear men will slight the Way and let it fall into disuse."

units.zh: 太子曰：「理旣有在，不容以人廢言，而況中賢之才，弘上聖之教，寧有壅塞之嫌？」
units.en: The crown prince said: "The principle stands—you cannot throw away the words because of the man; and when a middling talent spreads the highest Sage's teaching, is there any fear of blockage?"
units.literal: The crown prince said: "Since the principle exists, one cannot discard the words because of the man—and when a man of middling talent spreads the teaching of the highest Sage, could there be any suspicion of obstruction?"

units.zh: 臨川王映諮曰：「孝爲德本，常是所疑。
units.en: The prince of Linchuan, Xiao Ying, asked: "Filial piety as the root of virtue is often doubted.
units.literal: The prince of Linchuan, Xiao Ying, addressed him: "Filial piety as the root of virtue is often in doubt.

units.zh: 德施萬善，孝由天性，自然之理，豈因積習？」
units.en: Virtue pours into ten thousand goods; filial piety comes from inborn nature—the way of what is so. How could it rest on long practice?"
units.literal: Virtue extends to ten thousand goods; filial piety springs from inborn nature—it is the law of what is natural. How could it depend on accumulated habit?"

units.zh: 太子曰：「不因積習而至，所以可爲德本。」
units.en: The crown prince said: "It is because it is not reached by practice that it can be the root of virtue."
units.literal: The crown prince said: "Precisely because it is not reached through accumulated habit that it can serve as the root of virtue."

units.zh: 映曰：「率由斯至，不俟明德，大孝榮親，衆德光備，以此而言，豈得爲本？」
units.en: Ying said: "Follow this and you arrive without waiting for bright virtue; great filial piety honors kin and every virtue gleams—on that reading, how is it the root?"
units.literal: Ying said: "Following this one arrives without awaiting bright virtue; great filial piety brings glory to one's parents and all virtues shine complete—for that reason, how can it be called the root?"

units.zh: 太子曰：「孝有深淺，德有小大，因其分而爲本，何所稍疑？」
units.en: The crown prince said: "Filial piety has depth and shallowness, virtue has large and small—each takes its measure as root; what is left to doubt?"
units.literal: The crown prince said: "Filial piety has depth and shallowness, virtue has small and great—taking one's portion as root, what room for doubt remains?"

units.zh: 太子以長年臨學，亦前代未有也。
units.en: A crown prince of mature years presiding over the academy was likewise unheard of in earlier times.
units.literal: That the crown prince in mature years should preside over the academy was likewise without precedent in former ages.

units.zh: 明年，上將訊丹陽所領囚，及南北二百里內獄，詔曰：「獄訟之重，政化所先。
units.en: The next year the emperor was to hear cases for prisoners under Danyang and jails within two hundred li north and south, and decreed: "The weight of prison and suit comes first in rule and reform.
units.literal: The following year the emperor was to review prisoners under Danyang's jurisdiction and jails within two hundred li north and south, and issued an edict: "The weight of imprisonment and litigation comes first in government and transformation.

units.zh: 太子立年作貳，宜時詳覽，此訊事委以親決。」
units.en: The crown prince has come to years as second heir; he should look through these in good time—this hearing is entrusted to his own judgment."
units.literal: The crown prince has reached the years to serve as second to the throne; he should review these matters in timely detail—this review is entrusted to him for personal decision."

units.zh: 太子乃於玄圃園宣猷堂錄三署囚，原宥各有差。
units.en: The crown prince then, in the Hall of Proclaimed Teachings in the Mystic Enclosure Garden, entered the prisoners of the three offices and granted pardon each in measure.
units.literal: The crown prince then, in the Hall of Proclaimed Teachings in the Mystic Enclosure Garden, recorded prisoners from the three offices and granted pardons each according to degree.

units.zh: 上晚年好游宴，尚書曹事亦分送太子省視。
units.en: In his later years the emperor loved feasts and tours; Secretariat business was also split off and sent to the crown prince to review.
units.literal: In his later years the emperor favored feasts and outings; business from the Secretariat offices was also divided and sent to the crown prince for review.

units.zh: 太子與竟陵王子良俱好釋氏，立六疾館以養窮民。
units.en: The crown prince and the prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, both favored the Buddhist teaching and founded the Six Diseases Hospices to nourish the poor.
units.literal: The crown prince and the prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, both favored Buddhism and established the Six Diseases Hospices to care for the destitute.

units.zh: 風韻甚和而性頗奢麗，宮內殿堂，皆雕飾精綺，過於上宮。
units.en: His manner was gracious and easy, yet he was extravagant by nature; halls and chambers throughout his palace were carved and hung with fine brocade, outdoing even the emperor's own quarters.
units.literal: His bearing was very harmonious, yet his nature was rather luxurious; within the palace, every hall and chamber was carved and adorned with fine brocade, surpassing the upper palace.

units.zh: 開拓玄圃園，與臺城北塹等，其中樓觀塔宇，多聚奇石，妙極山水。
units.en: He laid out the Mystic Enclosure Garden to rival the capital's north moat; pavilions, belvederes, and pagodas rose among heaps of curious stone, the landscape wrought to a pitch of artifice.
units.literal: He opened and extended the Mystic Enclosure Garden, equal to the north moat of Jiankang; within it, towers, belvederes, and pagodas gathered many strange stones, achieving landscape to the utmost of wonder.

units.zh: 慮上宮望見，乃傍門列脩竹，內施高鄣，造游牆數百間，施諸機巧：宜須鄣蔽，須臾成立；
units.en: Lest the imperial palace look down upon it, he lined the gates with tall bamboo, raised high screens within, and built hundreds of touring wall-panels fitted with clever devices—when a screen was wanted, it rose in an instant;
units.literal: Fearing the upper palace might see it, he planted tall bamboo beside the gates, set high screens within, and built hundreds of movable wall-sections fitted with every sort of mechanism: when screening was needed, they stood up in a moment;

units.zh: 若應毀撤，應手遷徙。
units.en: when they were to come down, they moved aside at a touch.
units.literal: if they were to be taken down, they shifted away at a touch.

units.zh: 善制珍玩之物，織孔雀毛爲裘，光彩金翠，過於雉頭矣。
units.en: He excelled at precious novelties and wove peacock down into robes whose gold-green sheen outshone even zhichidou fur.
units.literal: He was skilled at making rare curios; he wove peacock feathers into robes whose gold-green brilliance surpassed even zhichidou fur.

units.zh: 以晉明帝爲太子時立西池，乃啓世祖引前例，求東田起小苑，上許之。
units.en: Citing the precedent of Jin Emperor Ming's Western Pool when he was heir, he petitioned Shizu to build a small park on the Eastern Fields; the emperor assented.
units.literal: Because when Emperor Ming of Jin was crown prince he had built the Western Pool, he memorialized Shizu citing that precedent and asked to raise a small park on the Eastern Fields; the emperor granted it.

units.zh: 永明中，二宮兵力全實，太子使宮中將吏更番役築，宮城苑巷，制度之盛，觀者傾京師。
units.en: During Yongming, both palaces kept their forces at full strength; the crown prince rotated palace officers through corvée labor on his works—palace wards, parks, and lanes—until the scale of the layout made the whole capital gape.
units.literal: In the Yongming era, both palaces' military strength stood at full muster; the crown prince had palace officers and clerks take turns on corvée to build—within the palace city, parks and lanes—the splendor of the layout made all Jiankang stare.

units.zh: 上性雖嚴，多布耳目，太子所爲，無敢啓者。
units.en: The emperor was stern by nature and kept many informants, yet no one dared speak of what the crown prince was doing.
units.literal: Though the emperor's nature was severe and he posted many eyes and ears, none dared report what the crown prince did.

units.zh: 後上幸豫章王宅，還過太子東田，見其彌亘華遠，莊麗極目，於是大怒，收監作主帥；
units.en: Later the emperor called on the prince of Yuzhang; returning by way of the crown prince's Eastern Fields, he saw splendor stretching without end, gorgeous to the horizon, and in a rage had the project overseers seized and jailed;
units.literal: Later, when the emperor visited the Prince of Yuzhang's residence and on his return passed the crown prince's Eastern Fields, he saw them sprawling in splendor, magnificent to the horizon, and in great wrath arrested and imprisoned the overseers in charge;

units.zh: 太子懼，皆藏匿之，由是見責。
units.en: the crown prince, afraid, hid them all away—and was rebuked for it.
units.literal: the crown prince, in fear, hid them all away and was rebuked for it.

units.zh: 太子素多疾，體又過壯，常在宮內，簡於遨遊。
units.en: The crown prince had long been sickly, yet his body was overfull; he kept to the inner palace and went little abroad.
units.literal: The crown prince had long been prone to illness, yet his frame was overly stout; he often stayed within the palace and was sparing in outings.

units.zh: 玩弄羽儀，多所僭儗，雖咫尺宮禁，而上終不知。
units.en: He toyed with regalia and overstepped rank in many ways; the palace forbidden zone was only steps away, yet the emperor never learned of it.
units.literal: He played with insignia of rank and usurped many prerogatives; though the forbidden precinct lay only a few paces away, the emperor never knew.

units.zh: 十年，豫章王嶷薨，太子見上友于旣至，造碑文奏之，未及鐫勒。
units.en: In the tenth year the prince of Yuzhang, Xiao Ni, died; seeing the emperor's brotherly love at its fullest, the crown prince drafted an epitaph and submitted it, but it had not yet been cut in stone.
units.literal: In the tenth year, the Prince of Yuzhang, Xiao Ni, died; the crown prince, seeing the emperor's brotherly affection had reached its height, composed an epitaph and presented it, but it was not yet carved.

units.zh: 十一年春正月，太子有疾，上自臨視，有憂色。
units.en: In the first month of spring of the eleventh year the crown prince fell ill; the emperor visited him in person, worry plain on his face.
units.literal: In the first month of spring in the eleventh year, the crown prince fell ill; the emperor came in person to visit him, his face troubled.

units.zh: 疾篤，上表曰：「臣地屬元良，業微三善，光道樹風，於焉蓋闕，晨宵忷懼，有若臨淵。
units.en: As the sickness deepened he memorialized: "I hold the heir's station, yet my fulfillment of the three duties is slight; to brighten the Way and set the tone for the realm—there I have failed; dawn to dusk I tremble as at a cliff's edge.
units.literal: When the illness turned grave, he submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant stands in the place of the heir, yet my achievement in the three duties is slight; to illumine the Way and plant custom—there I am wanting; morning and night I am anxious, as one standing over an abyss.

units.zh: 攝生舛和，構離痾疾，大漸惟幾，顧陰待謝。
units.en: In keeping my health I fell out of balance and brought on this lingering malady; the great change draws near, only a breath remains; I face the shade and wait to go.
units.literal: In tending my life I lost harmony and drew on myself this wasting illness; the great transition is near, only a little remains; I turn toward shadow and await departure.

units.zh: 守器難永，視膳長違，仰戀慈顏，內懷感哽。
units.en: To keep the vessel is not for long; to watch over your meals I must forever forgo; I lift my eyes to your gracious countenance and my throat closes with grief.
units.literal: To guard the vessel long is hard; to attend your meals will be forever denied; looking up I yearn for your kindly face, and within I choke with grief.

units.zh: 竊惟死生定分，理不足悲，伏願割無已之悼，損旣往之傷，寶衛聖躬，同休七百，臣雖沒九泉，無所遺恨。」
units.en: Yet I know life and death are allotted and need not be mourned; I beg you end grief without measure and ease sorrow for what has passed, guard your sacred person, and share fortune for seven hundred years—though I go down to the nine springs, I shall have no regret."
units.literal: I reflect that life and death are fixed allotments and reason gives no cause for grief; I humbly pray you cut off unending mourning and lessen grief for what is past, treasure and guard your sacred person, share blessing for seven hundred years—even if your servant sinks to the nine springs, no regret will remain."

units.zh: 時年三十六。
units.en: He was thirty-six.
units.literal: He was thirty-six years old.

units.zh: 太子年始過立，久在儲宮，得參政事；
units.en: The crown prince had only just come of age for investiture; long resident in the Eastern Palace, he had already shared in affairs of state;
units.literal: The crown prince had only just passed the age of investiture; long in the Eastern Palace, he had taken part in government affairs;

units.zh: 內外百司，咸謂旦暮繼體。
units.en: inside and outside the court, every office assumed he would succeed any day.
units.literal: within and without, every office held that he would succeed before long.

units.zh: 及薨，朝野驚惋焉。
units.en: When he died, court and country were shaken with grief.
units.literal: When he died, court and country were struck with shock and regret.

units.zh: 上幸東宮，臨哭盡哀，詔斂以袞冕之服，諡曰文惠，葬崇安陵。
units.en: The emperor came to the Eastern Palace and mourned with full grief; he ordered the heir enshrouded in full regalia, posthumously titled him Wenhui, and buried him at Chong'an Mausoleum.
units.literal: The emperor came to the Eastern Palace and wept there with full grief; he ordered him enshrouded in full ceremonial robes, gave the posthumous title Wenhui, and buried him at Chong'an Mausoleum.

units.zh: 世祖履行東宮，見太子服翫過制，大怒，勑有司隨事毀除，以東田殿堂爲崇虛館。
units.en: Shizu walked through the Eastern Palace, saw the crown prince's dress and playthings far past statute, and in a rage ordered the offices to demolish them on the spot; the Eastern Fields halls became the Chongxu Lodge.
units.literal: Shizu inspected the Eastern Palace, saw the crown prince's garments and curios beyond regulation, and in great anger ordered the offices to destroy them as found and made the Eastern Fields halls into the Chongxu Lodge.

units.zh: 鬱林立，追尊爲文帝，廟稱世宗。
units.en: When Yulin took the throne, he was posthumously honored as Emperor Wen, with the temple name Shizong.
units.literal: When Yulin was established, he was posthumously honored as Emperor Wen; his temple title was Shizong.

units.zh: 初，太子內懷惡明帝，密謂竟陵王子良曰：「我意色中殊不悅此人，當由其福德薄所致。」
units.en: Earlier the crown prince had secretly loathed Emperor Ming and told the prince of Jingling, Ziliang: "Something in my heart utterly rejects this man—surely his merit is thin."
units.literal: Earlier, the crown prince inwardly hated Emperor Ming and secretly told the Prince of Jingling, Ziliang: "In my heart I am wholly displeased with this man—it must be because his fortune is thin."

units.zh: 子良便苦救解。
units.en: Ziliang then begged hard that he be spared.
units.literal: Ziliang then pleaded earnestly to spare him.

units.zh: 後明帝立，果大相誅害。
units.en: Later, when Emperor Ming acceded, he did indeed kill on a vast scale.
units.literal: Later, when Emperor Ming took the throne, he indeed slaughtered many on a great scale.

units.zh: 史臣曰：上古之世，父不哭子。
units.en: The historian writes: In high antiquity a father did not mourn his son.
units.literal: The historian writes: In high antiquity, a father did not weep for his son.

units.zh: 壽夭悠悠，尚嗟恆事。
units.en: Life long or short drifts on—yet even that men still mourn as the common way.
units.literal: Long or short, life drifts on—yet even that we still lament as the common lot.

units.zh: 況夫正體東儲，方樹年德；
units.en: How much more when the rightful heir in the Eastern Palace was only beginning to grow in years and virtue;
units.literal: How much more the legitimate heir in the Eastern Palace, just setting out his years and virtue;

units.zh: 重基累葉，載茂皇家；
units.en: foundation laid generation on generation, glory heaped on the royal line;
units.literal: a foundation laid through generations, glory heaped on the imperial house;

units.zh: 守器之君，已知耕稼，雖溫文具美，交弘盛迹，武運將終，先期夙殞，傳之幼少，以速顛危。
units.en: an heir who already knew the plough—though his gentle learning was full and he shared in a flourishing age, the martial fortune was ending, he died before his season, and rule passed to a child, hastening collapse.
units.literal: a lord who guarded the vessel and already knew the plough—though gentle learning and letters were complete, and he joined in spreading a great record, the martial fortune was near its end, he perished early before his time, and the succession passed to the young, hastening ruin.

units.zh: 推此而論，亦有冥數矣。
units.en: Reasoned thus far, there is doom in the unseen too.
units.literal: Pushed to this conclusion, there is fate in the dark as well.

units.zh: 贊曰：二象垂則，三星麗天。
units.en: In praise: The two emblems hang as law; three stars crown the sky.
units.literal: In praise: The two images hang as law; the three stars adorn heaven.

units.zh: 樹嫡惟長，義匪求賢。
units.en: The heir is set by birth order alone; right does not mean choosing the worthy.
units.literal: The heir is planted by seniority alone; the principle is not to seek worth.

units.zh: 方爲守器，植命不延。
units.en: He had only just become keeper of the vessel; the life planted would not run its course.
units.literal: He had just become keeper of the vessel; the life planted would not extend.

units.zh: 後爲晉平王左常侍，遷司空桂陽王行參軍，隨齊司空柳世隆守郢城，拒荊州刺史沈攸之。
units.en: He became regular attendant to the Prince of Jinping, then staff officer to the Prince of Guiyang under the Minister of Works, and followed Liu Shilong in the defense of Yingcheng against Shen Youzhi.
units.literal: Later he was Regular Attendant to the Prince of Jinping, then a staff officer on the Prince of Guiyang's suite under the Minister of Works; he followed Qi Minister of Works Liu Shilong in holding Yingcheng against Jingzhou Inspector Shen Youzhi.

units.zh: 攸之平，遷前軍中兵參軍。
units.en: After Youzhi's defeat he was made army aide of the van.
units.literal: When Youzhi was pacified, he was promoted to Army Aide of the Van.

units.zh: 時明帝謀入嗣位，朝之舊臣皆引參謀策。
units.en: Mingdi was then plotting to enter the succession; old courtiers were all drawn into counsel.
units.literal: Mingdi was then plotting succession to the throne; old ministers of the court were all drawn into counsel.

units.zh: 明帝下詔曰：「夫超然榮觀，風流自遠；
units.en: Mingdi issued an edict: "To stand beyond glory is to see the world from far off;
units.literal: Mingdi issued an edict: "One who stands apart from glory views the world from afar;

units.zh: 初，齊明帝及覽父綍、東海徐孝嗣，並爲吳興，號稱名守，覽皆欲過之！
units.en: Once Qi Mingdi, Lan's father Fu, and Donghai's Xu Xiaosi had all ruled Wuxing as famed administrators—Lan meant to outdo them all!
units.literal: Earlier Qi Mingdi, Lan's father Fu, and Xu Xiaosi of Donghai had all governed Wuxing and been called famed administrators—Lan wished to surpass them all!

units.zh: 建武四年，詔徵爲侍中、中書令，遂抗表不應召。
units.en: In Jianwu's fourth year an edict summoned him as attendant-in-ordinary and palace secretariat director; he memorialized and refused.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwu an edict summoned him as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Palace Secretariat Director; he submitted a memorial refusing the summons.

units.zh: 蹈彼幽人，英華罕值。
units.en: to walk the hermit's way is to bloom in solitude.
units.literal: one who treads the hermit's path is rarely met in full flower.

units.zh: 故長揖楚相，見稱南國；
units.en: hence the long bow of the Chu minister won praise in the southern states;
units.literal: Hence the long bow to the Chu minister won praise in the southern states;

units.zh: 高謝漢臣，取貴良史。
units.en: the Han worthy's lofty refusal won honor from fine historians.
units.literal: the Han worthy's high refusal won honor from fine historians.

units.zh: 新除侍中、中書令朏，早藉羽儀，夙標清尚，登朝樹績，出守馳聲。
units.en: The newly appointed attendant-in-ordinary and palace secretariat director Fei long wore court insignia and from youth bore a clear name; in court he built merit, abroad he made his name heard.
units.literal: The newly appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Palace Secretariat Director Fei long bore the court insignia and from youth bore a pure reputation; in court he built merit, going out he made his name heard.

units.zh: 遂斂跡康衢，拂衣林沚，抱箕潁之餘芳，甘憔悴而無悶。
units.en: Then he gathered his steps from the broad highway and shook dust from forest robes, keeping the after-scent of Jiqian and Ying, glad in lean exile without regret.
units.literal: Then he gathered his steps from the broad highway and shook the dust from his forest robes, embracing the lingering fragrance of Jiqian and Ying, content in lean exile without regret.

units.zh: 撫事懷人，載留欽想。
units.en: Hearing his story, one keeps him in honored thought.
units.literal: Hearing of his deeds one keeps him in honored thought.

units.zh: 宜加優禮，用旌素概。
units.en: Let added courtesy mark his plain integrity.
units.literal: He should receive added courtesy to mark his plain integrity.

units.zh: 可賜床帳褥席，俸以卿祿，常出在所。」
units.en: Grant bed curtains and padded mats, salary at minister rank, always sent to his dwelling."
units.literal: Grant bed curtains and padded mats, salary at minister rank, always provided at his dwelling."

units.zh: 武穆裴皇后諱惠昭，河東聞喜人也。
units.en: Empress Wumu Pei Huizhao came from Wenxi in Hedong commandery.
units.literal: Empress Wumu of the Pei clan, taboo name Huizhao, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong.

units.zh: 諡穆妃，葬休安陵。
units.en: She was posthumously titled Consort Mu and buried at Xiu'an Mausoleum.
units.literal: She was given the posthumous title Consort Mu and buried at Xiu'an Mausoleum.

units.zh: 宋世，太祖為文惠太子納后，桂陽賊至，太祖在新亭，傳言已沒，宅復為人所抄掠，文惠太子、竟陵王子良奉穆后、庾妃及后挺身送后兄昺之家，事平乃出。
units.en: In the Song era the Grand Ancestor took her in marriage for Crown Prince Wenhui. When the Guiyang rebels came, the Grand Ancestor was at Xinting; rumor said he had perished, and the residence was plundered again. Crown Prince Wenhui and Prince of Jingling Ziliang, escorting Empress Mu, Lady Yu, and the empress, risked themselves to take them to the empress's brother Bing's house; when order was restored they came out.
units.literal: In the Song age the Grand Ancestor received the empress in marriage for Crown Prince Wenhui. When the Guiyang rebels arrived, the Grand Ancestor was at Xinting; rumor spread that he had perished, and the residence was again plundered. Crown Prince Wenhui and Prince of Jingling Ziliang, escorting Empress Mu, Lady Yu, and the empress, braved danger to deliver them to the empress's brother Bing's house; when the affair was settled they emerged.

units.zh: 昇明三年，為齊世子妃。
units.en: In Shengming year 3 she became consort to the Qi heir apparent.
units.literal: In the third year of Shengming she became consort to the Qi heir apparent.

units.zh: 建元元年，為皇太子妃。
units.en: In the first year of Jianyuan she became consort to the crown prince.
units.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan she became consort to the crown prince.

units.zh: 世祖即位，追尊皇后。
units.en: When Shizong acceded she was posthumously honored as empress.
units.literal: When Shizong took the throne she was posthumously honored as empress.

units.zh: 父璣之，左軍參軍。
units.en: Her father Pei Jizhi had been a left-army aide.
units.literal: Her father Jizhi was a left-army aide.

units.zh: 祖朴之，給事中。
units.en: Her grandfather Pei Puzhi had been a palace attendant.
units.literal: Her grandfather Puzhi was a palace attendant.

units.zh: 贈璣之金紫光祿大夫，后母檀氏餘杭廣昌鄉元君。
units.en: Pei Jizhi was made household minister with the purple-gold seal, and the empress's mother, née Tan, Village Lady of Guangchang in Yuhang.
units.literal: Jizhi was given the post of household minister with the purple-gold seal; the empress's mother, the Tan clan, was made Village Lady of Guangchang in Yuhang.

units.zh: 三年，后薨。
units.en: In year 3 the empress died.
units.literal: In the third year the empress died.

units.zh: 性剛嚴，竟陵王子良妃袁氏布衣時有過，后加訓罰。
units.en: She was stern and strict by nature; when Yuan, consort of Prince of Jingling Ziliang, blundered while still a commoner, the empress rebuked and punished her.
units.literal: By nature stern and strict; when Yuan, consort of Prince of Jingling Ziliang, erred while still a commoner, the empress added reproof and punishment.

units.zh: 尚書敬顯儁曰：「孔子云：『微管仲，吾其被發左衽矣』以此言之，右衽為是。」
units.en: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."
units.literal: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."

units.zh: 臨川內史王觀，僧虔之孫，人身不惡，便可召爲長史，以代元沖。」
units.en: Linchuan interior administrator Wang Guan, Sengqian's grandson, is not ill-favored—summon him as chief clerk for Yuanchong."
units.literal: Linchuan interior administrator Wang Guan, grandson of Sengqian, is not ill-favored in person—call him in as chief clerk to replace Yuanchong."

units.zh: 俄而荊州刺史沈攸之作亂，高帝謂淹曰：「天下紛紛若是，君謂何如？」
units.en: Soon Jing inspector Shen Youzhi rose in arms; Gaodi asked Yan, "The world is chaos like this—what is your view?"
units.literal: Before long Jing inspector Shen Youzhi rebelled; Gaodi said to Yan, "The realm is in such turmoil—what do you think?"

units.zh: 昇明初，齊帝輔政，聞其才，召爲尚書駕部郎、驃騎參軍事。
units.en: At the start of Ascendant Bright, with Qi's emperor as regent, he heard of Yan and made him secretariat director of the imperial equipage and valiant-cavalry staff officer.
units.literal: At the start of the Ascendant Bright era, when Qi's emperor held regency, he heard of Yan's talent and summoned him as Masters of Writing director of the imperial equipage and valiant-cavalry staff officer.

units.zh: 太祖高皇帝篤猶子之愛，降家人之慈；
units.en: Grand Ancestor Gao cherished a nephew as a son and gave the kindness of kin under one roof;
units.literal: Grand Ancestor Emperor Gao cherished the love due a nephew-son and granted the kindness shown within a household;

units.zh: 立皇子嶷爲豫章王，映爲臨川王，晃爲長沙王，曅爲武陵王，暠爲安成王，鏘爲鄱陽王，鑠爲桂陽王，鑒爲廣陵王，皇孫長懋爲南郡王。
units.en: Princes were named: Yi of Yuzhang, Ying of Linchuan, Huang of Changsha, Ye of Wuling, Gao of Ancheng, Qiang of Poyang, Shuo of Guiyang, Jian of Guangling; the imperial grandson Zhangmao became prince of Nan commandery.
units.literal: The princes Luan was made Prince of Yuzhang; Ying Prince of Linchuan; Huang Prince of Changsha; Ye Prince of Wuling; Gao Prince of Ancheng; Qiang Prince of Poyang; Shuo Prince of Guiyang; Jian Prince of Guangling; the imperial grandson Zhangmao Prince of Nan.

units.zh: 以後將軍長沙王晃爲護軍將軍，中軍將軍南郡王長懋爲南徐州刺史，冠軍將軍安成王暠爲江州刺史。
units.en: Prince of Changsha Xiao Huang, rear general, became protector of the army; Prince of Nan Commandery Xiao Zhangmao, general of the center, took South Xuzhou; Prince of Ancheng Xiao Gao, champion general, took Jiang.
units.literal: Rear General, Prince of Changsha Xiao Huang was made Protector of the Army; General of the Center, Prince of Nan Commandery Xiao Changmao was made Inspector of South Xuzhou; Champion General, Prince of Ancheng Xiao Hao was made Inspector of Jiang.

units.zh: 戊戌，以荊州刺史嶷爲尚書令、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、揚州刺史，冠軍將軍映爲荊州刺史，西中郎將晃爲南徐州刺史，冠軍將軍垣崇祖爲豫州刺史，驃騎司馬崔文仲爲徐州刺史。
units.en: Day wuxu: Yi, inspector of Jing, became director of the master of writing, general-in-chief who spreads might, with secretariat equal to the three excellencies, and inspector of Yang; Ying, champion general, inspector of Jing; Huang, west general of the gentlemen, inspector of South Xuzhou; Yuan Chongzu, champion general, inspector of Yu; Cui Wenzong, chief commandant under the general who spreads might, inspector of Xu.
units.literal: On day wuxu, Inspector of Jing Province Luan was made Director of the Master of Writing, General-in-Chief Who Spreads Might, with Grand Secretariat and staff equal to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Yang Province; General Who Vanquishes the Foe Ying was made Inspector of Jing Province; West General of the Gentlemen Huang was made Inspector of South Xuzhou; General Who Vanquishes the Foe Yuan Chongzu was made Inspector of Yu Province; Chief Commandant of the General Who Spreads Might Cui Wenzong was made Inspector of Xu Province.

units.zh: 乙巳，以新除尚書令、驃騎將軍豫章王嶷爲荊、湘二州刺史，平西將軍臨川王映爲揚州刺史。
units.en: Day yisi: Yi, new director of the master of writing and general who spreads might, prince of Yuzhang, took Jing and Xiang; Ying, prince of Linchuan and general who pacifies the west, took Yang.
units.literal: On day yisi the newly appointed Director of the Master of Writing, General-in-Chief Who Spreads Might, Prince of Yuzhang Luan was made Inspector of Jing and Xiang; General Who Pacifies the West, Prince of Linchuan Ying was made Inspector of Yang.

units.zh: 壬子，以驃騎大將軍豫章王嶷爲司空，揚州刺史、前將軍臨川王映爲荊州刺史。
units.en: On day renzi, Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Yi, general of agile cavalry, became minister of works; Prince of Linchuan Xiao Ying, forward general and inspector of Yangzhou, took Jing.
units.literal: On day renzi, General of Agile Cavalry, Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Luan was made Minister of Works; Inspector of Yangzhou, Forward General, Prince of Linchuan Xiao Ying was made Inspector of Jing.

units.zh: 梁州刺史范柏年被誅，其親將李烏奴懼奔叛，文弘納之。
units.en: Fan Bonian, inspector of Liangzhou, was executed; his trusted officer Li Wunu, fearing for his life, fled in rebellion, and Wenhong took him in.
units.literal: The Inspector of Liangzhou Fan Bonian was executed; his close general Li Wunu feared and fled in rebellion; Wenhong received him.

units.zh: 梁州刺史范柏年懷挾詭態，首鼠兩端，旣已被伐，盤桓稽命。
units.en: Fan Bonian, inspector of Liangzhou, harbored treacherous designs and wavered between two sides; though already punished, he lingered and delayed his end.
units.literal: The Inspector of Liangzhou Fan Bonian harbored deceitful attitudes, was a rat with head to both ends; having already been punished, he lingered and delayed his fate.

units.zh: 柏年今已梟禽，烏奴頻被摧破，計其餘燼，行自消夷。
units.en: Bonian has already been executed; Wunu has been repeatedly defeated—their remaining embers will soon die out on their own.
units.literal: Bonian has now been beheaded and captured; Wunu has repeatedly been shattered and broken—reckoning their remaining embers, they will soon extinguish of themselves.

units.zh: 遂潛遣李烏奴叛。
units.en: He then secretly sent Li Wunu into rebellion.
units.literal: He then secretly sent Li Wunu to rebel.

units.zh: 夫曾參以布衣猶難之，今陛下親以王者修之，過曾參遠矣。
units.en: Even Zeng Shen, a commoner, struggled to match such devotion; you did it as heir to a kingdom—you have outdone Zeng Shen by a wide margin.
units.literal: Even Zeng Shen in plain cloth still found that hard; now Your Majesty, in the person of a king, practiced it—you surpass Zeng Shen by far.

units.zh: 永明初，衛將軍王儉領丹陽尹，復引爲主簿。
units.en: Early in Yongming, Wang Jian of the guards, as Danyang intendant, drew him back as chief clerk.
units.literal: Early Yongming, General of the Guards Wang Jian took Danyang as intendant and again recruited him as chief clerk.

units.zh: 鄭玄字康成，北海高密人也。
units.en: Zheng Xuan, style Kangcheng, came from Gaomi in Beihai commandery.
units.literal: Zheng Xuan, courtesy name Kangcheng, was a native of Gaomi in Beihai.

units.zh: 休見而嘆曰：『康成入吾室，操吾矛，以伐我乎！』
units.en: He Xiu exclaimed: "Kangcheng is in my room, wielding my own spear against me!"
units.literal: When Xiu saw this he sighed and said: 'Kangcheng has entered my chamber, taken my spear, and come to attack me!'

units.zh: 玄少為鄉嗇夫，得休歸，嘗詣學官，不樂為吏，父數怒之，不能禁。
units.en: As a youth he was a township clerk; on leave he visited the local school, found clerking distasteful, and though his father berated him repeatedly could not change his mind.
units.literal: In his youth Xuan was village clerk for his township; when he had leave to return home he once visited the school official, disliked being a clerk, and his father repeatedly grew angry with him but could not stop him.

units.zh: 融素驕貴，玄在門下，三年不得見，乃使高業弟子傳授於玄。
units.en: Ma Rong was haughty by nature; Zheng Xuan studied at his gate three years without an interview and learned only through Ma's senior pupils.
units.literal: Rong by nature was proud and lofty; Xuan was in his gate for three years without being granted an audience, and Rong therefore had advanced disciples transmit the teaching to Xuan.

units.zh: 玄日夜尋誦，未嘗怠倦。
units.en: Zheng Xuan read day and night without slackening.
units.literal: Xuan day and night pursued recitation and never slackened.

units.zh: 會融集諸生考論圖緯，聞玄善算，乃召見於樓上，玄因從質諸疑義，問畢辭歸。
units.en: When Ma Rong gathered his students to debate charts and weft-books, he heard Zheng Xuan excelled at reckoning and summoned him upstairs; Zheng exhausted his doubts, then bowed out and left.
units.literal: When Rong assembled the disciples to examine and debate the charts and weft-texts, he heard that Xuan was skilled in calculation and therefore summoned him to an audience in the upper story; Xuan thereupon questioned him on all doubtful points, and when the questions were finished he took leave and returned.

units.zh: 玄自遊學，十餘年乃歸鄉裏。
units.en: More than ten years passed in wandering study before he went home.
units.literal: From the time Xuan traveled for study, more than ten years passed before he returned to his home village.

units.zh: 玄乃發《墨守》，針《膏肓》，起《廢疾》。
units.en: Zheng Xuan breached the Fortress, lanced the Vital Zone, and cured the Morbid Spots.
units.literal: Xuan thereupon cracked Mo shou, needled Gao huang, and revived Fei ji.

units.zh: 融喟然謂門人曰：『鄭生今去，吾道東矣。』
units.en: Ma Rong sighed to his disciples: "When Zheng goes east, my teaching travels with him."
units.literal: Rong sighed deeply and said to his disciples: 'When the Zheng student departs now, my way goes east.'

units.zh: 遂造太學受業，師事京兆第五元先，始通《京氏易》、《公羊春秋》、《三統歷》、《九章算術》。
units.en: He entered the imperial academy under Fifth Yuanxian of Jingzhao, mastering the Jing Changes, Gongyang Annals, Triple Concordance calendar, and Nine Chapters.
units.literal: He therefore went to the imperial academy to pursue studies, served as disciple to Fifth Yuanxian of the capital region, and first mastered the Jing lineage Changes, the Gongyang Spring and Autumn, the Triple Concordance calendar, and the Nine Chapters on mathematical procedures.

units.zh: 家貧，客耕東萊，學徒相隨已數百千人。
units.en: Poor, he farmed for hire in Donglai while hundreds and then thousands of pupils trailed after him.
units.literal: His family was poor; he hired out his plowing in Donglai, and students who followed him already numbered in the hundreds and thousands.

units.zh: 又從東郡張恭祖受《周官》、《禮記》、《左氏春秋》、《韓詩》、《古文尚書》。
units.en: From Zhang Gongzu of Dong he took the Rites of Zhou, Book of Rites, Zuo Annals, Han Odes, and old-text Documents.
units.literal: He further received from Zhang Gongzu of Dong commandery the Rites of Zhou, the Record of Rites, the Zuo Spring and Autumn, the Han Odes, and the old-text Documents.

units.zh: 以山東無兄問者，乃西入關，因涿郡盧植，事扶風馬融。
units.en: Finding no teacher of stature east of the mountains, he crossed into the west and, introduced by Lu Zhi of Zhu, studied under Ma Rong of Fufeng.
units.literal: Because east of the mountains there was no one he could consult, he went west through the passes, and through Lu Zhi of Zhuo commandery served Ma Rong of Fufeng.

units.zh: 初，中興之後，範升、陳元、李育、賈逵之徒爭論古今學，後馬融答北地太守劉瑰及玄答何休，義據通深，由是古學遂明。
units.en: Earlier, after Guangwu, Fan Sheng, Chen Yuan, Li Yu, and Jia Kui had wrangled old versus new learning; later Ma Rong answered Liu Gui, prefect of Beidi, and Zheng Xuan answered He Xiu—with such depth that old-text scholarship carried the day.
units.literal: At first, after the restoration, Fan Sheng, Chen Yuan, Li Yu, Jia Kui, and their sort debated old and new learning; later Ma Rong answered the grand administrator of Beidi Liu Gui and Xuan answered He Xiu—their arguments were thorough and deep, and thereby old-text learning became clear.

units.zh: 及黨事起，乃與同郡孫嵩等四十餘人俱被禁錮，遂隱修經業，杜門不出。
units.en: When the partisan proscription struck, he and forty-odd countrymen including Sun Song were banned from office; he shut his doors, deepened his textual studies, and stayed in.
units.literal: When the faction case arose, he together with more than forty men of his commandery such as Sun Song was all placed under prohibition, and he therefore retired to cultivate the classics behind closed doors and did not go out.

units.zh: 八世祖崇，哀帝時尚書仆射。
units.en: Eight generations back, Zheng Chong had been vice-director of the secretariat under Emperor Ai.
units.literal: Eight generations back his ancestor Chong was vice-director of the secretariat in the time of Emperor Ai.

units.zh: 太子曰：「顏子縮屋稱貞，柳下嫗而不亂，未若此翁白首不娶者也。」
units.en: The crown prince said, "Yan Hui was praised for chastity though he lived in a hovel, and Liu Xiahui kept his integrity though he shared a blanket with a woman—but neither can match this old man who has never married even to white hair."
units.literal: The crown prince said, "Yan Hui, who shrank in his hut, was called chaste; Liu Xiahui, who shared a blanket with a woman, was not corrupted—yet neither equals this old man, white-haired and never married."

units.zh: 王僧虔 張緒
units.en: Wang Sengqian; Zhang Xu
units.literal: Wang Sengqian; Zhang Xu

units.zh: 南齊書卷三十三‧列傳第十四
units.en: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 33 — Biography 14
units.literal: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 33 — Biography 14

units.zh: 順皇帝諱準，字仲謀，[1]小字智觀，明帝第三子也。
units.en: Emperor Shun, taboo name Zhun, courtesy name Zhongmou, [1] childhood name Zhiguan, was the third son of Emperor Ming.
units.literal: Emperor Shun, taboo name Zhun, courtesy name Zhongmou, [1] childhood name Zhiguan, was the third son of Emperor Ming.

units.zh: 遷司徒刑獄參軍事，入爲尚書殿中郎，轉司徒竟陵王記室參軍，以父憂去職。
units.en: He rose to prison staff in the criminal office, then palace attendant in the secretariat, then recorder to the Prince of Jingling, and left for his father's mourning.
units.literal: Promoted to Criminal Office Prison staff officer, entered as Attendant of the Palace Department in the Masters of Writing, then transferred to Staff Officer and Recorder to the Prince of Jingling of the Secretariat, left office for father's mourning.

units.zh: 始高祖與昉遇竟陵王西邸，從容謂昉曰：「我登三府，當以卿爲記室。」
units.en: When Gaozu first met Fang at the Prince of Jingling's western residence, he said lightly, "When I reach the three offices, you shall be my recorder."
units.literal: When Gaozu first met Fang at the Prince of Jingling's Western Residence, he said with ease: "When I rise to the three offices, I shall make you my recorder."

units.zh: 父顒，齊中書侍郎，有名於時。
units.en: His father Yan had been a Secretariat Attendant under Qi and was well known in his day.
units.literal: His father Yan was a Secretariat Attendant of Qi and had a reputation in his time.

units.zh: 周捨字昇逸，汝南安城人，晉左光祿大夫顗之八世孫也。
units.en: Zhou She, whose courtesy name was Shengyi, came from Ancheng in Runan and was the eighth-generation descendant of Zhou Yi, who had served Jin as Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
units.literal: Zhou She, styled Shengyi, was a native of Ancheng in Runan and an eighth-generation descendant of Zhou Yi, the Jin Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

units.zh: 捨幼聰潁，顒異之，臨卒謂曰：「汝不患不富貴，但當持之以道德。」
units.en: As a boy, She was quick and clever, and Yan saw something extraordinary in him. On his deathbed Yan told him, "You need not fear that you will lack wealth and rank, but you must hold yourself to moral principle."
units.literal: She in youth was clever and quick; Yan regarded him as exceptional. On his deathbed he told him, "You need not worry about lacking wealth and rank, but you must uphold yourself with moral virtue."

units.zh: 吏部尚書范雲與顒素善，重捨才器，言之於高祖，召拜尚書祠部郎。
units.en: Fan Yun, Minister of Personnel, had long been close to Yan and admired She's ability. He recommended him to the High Ancestor, who summoned She and appointed him Gentleman of the Sacrifices Section in the Secretariat.
units.literal: Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Fan Yun had long been on good terms with Yan and valued She's talent and capacity; he spoke of him to the High Ancestor, who summoned and appointed him Gentleman of the Department of Sacrifices in the Secretariat.

units.zh: 建元初，又爲驃騎豫章王記室，帶東武令，參掌詔册，並典國史。
units.en: At Jianyuan's opening he was again valiant-cavalry record-keeper to the Prince of Yuzhang, magistrate of Dongwu in addition, drafting edicts and patents and tending the national history.
units.literal: At the start of Jianyuan he was again valiant-cavalry record-keeper to the Prince of Yuzhang, with concurrent magistrate of Dongwu, charged with edicts and patents and also keeper of the national history.

units.zh: 辛亥，以安西將軍王玄邈爲中護軍，新除後軍司馬蕭誕爲徐州刺史。
units.en: Day xinhai: Wang Xuanmiao, pacifying-west general, became central colonel; Xiao Dan, newly made rear-army major, took Xuzhou.
units.literal: Day xinhai: Pacifying-West General Wang Xuanmiao was made Central Colonel; newly appointed Rear-Army Major Xiao Dan was made Inspector of Xuzhou.

units.zh: 於是江州刺史晉安王子懋起兵，遣中護軍王玄邈討之。
units.en: Then Xiao Zimao, prince of Jin'an and inspector of Jiangzhou, rose in arms; Wang Xuanmiao, central colonel, was sent against him.
units.literal: Thereupon Prince Zimao of Jin'an, Inspector of Jiangzhou, raised troops; Central Colonel Wang Xuanmiao was sent to attack him.

units.zh: 轉太祖平南府，晉熙王府參軍。
units.en: He was moved to the pacify-the-south headquarters and made staff officer in the Prince of Jinxi's household.
units.literal: He was shifted to the founding emperor's Pacify-the-South headquarters and staff officer of the Prince of Jinxi's mansion.

units.zh: 世祖武皇帝情等布衣，寄深同氣。
units.en: Ancestor Emperor Wu treated him as an equal of the robe and bound him with shared blood.
units.literal: Ancestor Emperor Wu treated him as a commoner's equal and entrusted him with the bond of shared blood.

units.zh: 武皇大漸，實奉詔言。
units.en: When Emperor Wu lay dying, I truly received his charge in words.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu fell gravely ill, I truly received his charge in words.

units.zh: 鬱林王昭業，字元尚，文惠太子長子也。
units.en: The Prince of Yulin, Zhaoye, bore the style Yuanshang and was the eldest son of Crown Prince Wenhui.
units.literal: The Prince of Yulin, Zhaoye, styled Yuanshang, was the eldest son of Crown Prince Wenhui.

units.zh: 小名法身。
units.en: In childhood he was called Fashen.
units.literal: His childhood name was Fashen.

units.zh: 王侯五日一問訊，世祖常獨呼昭業至幄座，別加撫問，呼爲法身，鍾愛甚重。
units.en: Princes and dukes attended court every five days, but Emperor Wu often summoned Zhaoye alone to the curtained seat for extra questioning, called him Fashen, and doted on him exceedingly.
units.literal: Princes and dukes paid court every five days; Emperor Wu would often call Zhaoye alone to the curtained seat and question him with special favor, calling him Fashen, and cherished him deeply.

units.zh: 鬱林王
units.en: Prince of Yulin
units.literal: Prince of Yulin

units.zh: 史臣曰：鬱林王風華外美，衆所同惑。
units.en: The historian writes: The Prince of Yulin wore grace on the outside, and everyone was taken in alike.
units.literal: The historian writes: The Prince of Yulin was outwardly fair in bearing, and all were deceived alike.

units.zh: 世祖卽位，封南郡王，二千戶。
units.en: When Emperor Wu ascended, he was made prince of Nan commandery with a fief of two thousand households.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nan commandery with two thousand households.

units.zh: 爲南郡王時，文惠太子禁其起居，節其用度，昭業謂豫章王妃庾氏曰：「阿婆，佛法言，有福德生帝王家。
units.en: As prince of Nan commandery, Crown Prince Wenhui controlled his movements and cut his allowance; Zhaoye told the princess of Yuzhang, Lady Yu: "Granny, the Buddha says those with merit and fortune are born into a royal house.
units.literal: When he was Prince of Nan commandery, Crown Prince Wenhui restricted his comings and goings and curbed his expenses; Zhaoye said to the Princess of Yuzhang, Lady Yu of the household: "Grandmother, Buddhist teaching says that those with merit and fortune are born into an imperial house.

units.zh: 文惠太子薨，立昭業爲皇太孫，居東宮。
units.en: After Crown Prince Wenhui died, Zhaoye was made imperial grandson-heir and moved into the Eastern Palace.
units.literal: When Crown Prince Wenhui died, Zhaoye was established as imperial grandson-heir and dwelt in the Eastern Palace.

units.zh: 帝在壽昌殿，聞外有變，使閉內殿諸房閣，令閹人登興光樓望，還報云：「見一人戎服，從數百人，急裝，在西鐘樓下。」
units.en: The emperor was in Shouchang Hall. Hearing trouble outside, he shut the inner halls and sent a eunuch up Xingguang Tower to look. The man came back and said, "I see one man in armor, with several hundred followers, armed in haste, below the Western Bell Tower."
units.literal: The emperor was in Shouchang Hall; hearing disturbance outside, he had the inner halls and chambers closed and ordered a eunuch to climb Xingguang Tower to look; returning he reported: "I see one man in battle dress, with several hundred men, armed in haste, below the Western Bell Tower."

units.zh: 世祖崩，太孫卽位。
units.en: When Emperor Wu died, the imperial grandson-heir ascended.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu died, the imperial grandson-heir took the throne.

units.zh: 昭業少美容止，好隸書，世祖勑皇孫手書不得妄出，以貴重之。
units.en: Zhaoye was handsome in youth and loved clerical script; Emperor Wu commanded that the great-grandson's hand must not circulate casually, holding it precious.
units.literal: Zhaoye in youth had a fine countenance and bearing and loved clerical script; Emperor Wu ordered that the imperial grandson's own writing must not be sent out rashly, treating it as precious.

units.zh: 十一月辛亥，立臨汝公昭文爲新安王，曲江公昭秀爲臨海王，皇弟昭粲爲永嘉王。
units.en: Eleventh month, day xinhai: Zhaowen, duke of Linru, became prince of Xin'an; Zhaoxiu, duke of Qujiang, prince of Linhai; the emperor's brother Zhaocan, prince of Yongjia.
units.literal: Eleventh month, day xinhai: Duke Zhaowen of Linru was established as Prince of Xin'an; Duke Zhaoxiu of Qujiang as Prince of Linhai; the emperor's younger brother Zhaocan as Prince of Yongjia.

units.zh: 冬十月壬寅，尊皇太孫太妃爲皇太后，立皇后何氏。
units.en: Winter, tenth month, day renyin: the great-grandson's mother was made empress dowager and Lady He was established as empress.
units.literal: Winter, tenth month, day renyin: The great-grandson's consort-mother was honored as empress dowager; Lady He was established as empress.

units.zh: 昭業與文帝幸姬霍氏淫通，龍駒勸長留宮內，聲云度霍氏爲尼，以餘人代之。
units.en: Zhaoye lay with Emperor Wen's favored lady, Lady Huo; Longju urged him to linger in the palace, saying he would have Lady Huo take the tonsure and put another in her place.
units.literal: Zhaoye had illicit relations with Emperor Wen's favored lady, Lady Huo; Longju urged him to stay long in the palace, claiming he would have Lady Huo tonsured as a nun and replace her with another.

units.zh: 須臾，蕭諶領兵先入宮，截壽昌閣，帝走向愛姬徐氏房，拔劔自刺不中，以帛纏頸，輿接出延德殿。
units.en: A moment later Xiao Chen led the van into the palace and sealed Shouchang Pavilion. The emperor fled to his favorite Lady Xu's room, drew a sword and missed his own throat, bound his neck in silk, and was borne out on a litter to Yande Hall.
units.literal: In a moment Xiao Chen led troops in first, cut off Shouchang Pavilion; the emperor ran toward his favorite Lady Xu's chamber, drew a sword and stabbed himself but missed, wrapped silk about his neck, and was carried out on a litter to Yande Hall.

units.zh: 永明五年十一月戊子，冠於東宮崇政殿。
units.en: Yongming 5, eleventh month, day wuzi: he received the cap in the Eastern Palace's Chongzheng Hall.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Yongming, eleventh month, day wuzi, he was capped in the Chongzheng Hall of the Eastern Palace.

units.zh: 隆昌元年春正月丁未，改元，大赦。
units.en: Longchang 1, spring, first month, day dingwei: the era was changed and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
units.literal: Longchang 1, spring, first month, day dingwei: the era name was changed and a general amnesty proclaimed.

units.zh: 鎮軍居正體道，家國是賴，伊霍之舉，實寄淵謨，便可詳依舊典，以禮廢黜。
units.en: The suppressing-army general holds to the upright Way; state and house depend on him; the act of Yi and Huo rests on grave design—follow the ancient precedents in full and remove him by ritual.
units.literal: The Suppressing-Army General stands upright in the Way; the state and clan rely on him; the deed of Yi and Huo rests truly on deep counsel—you may now follow the old statutes in detail and depose him by rite.

units.zh: 高宗慮變，定謀廢帝。
units.en: Fearing a coup, the High Ancestor set his mind to depose the emperor.
units.literal: The High Ancestor, fearing change, fixed a plan to depose the emperor.

units.zh: 出西弄，殺之，時年二十一，輿尸出徐龍駒宅，殯葬以王禮。
units.en: They took him to the Western Lane and killed him. He was twenty-one. His body was borne to Xu Longju's house and buried with the rites due a prince.
units.literal: He was taken out to the Western Lane and killed; he was twenty-one. The corpse was carried out to Xu Longju's house and buried with princely rites.

units.zh: 伏情隱詐，難以貌求。
units.en: He buried feeling and hid fraud; the face told you nothing.
units.literal: He hid feeling and concealed deceit—one could not seek him by appearance.

units.zh: 詔曰：「朕以寡薄，嗣膺寶政，對越靈命，欽若前圖，思所以敬守成規，拱揖羣后。
units.en: An edict said: "I am slight in virtue yet have taken up the throne, facing Heaven's mandate and following the models of old, seeking to keep the inherited order and yield the floor to you, my lords.
units.literal: An edict said: "I, of little worth, have succeeded to the imperial charge, facing the mandate of Heaven and revering the precedents of old, thinking how to reverently hold to established rules and bow to the assembled lords.

units.zh: 哀荒在日，有懵大猷，宜育德振民，光昭睿範。
units.en: I am still in the days of grief and the great plan is unclear to me; I must cultivate virtue and lift the people, and let a wise example shine.
units.literal: Days of mourning still lie before me, and the great design is dim; I should nurture virtue and steady the people, making bright the sage's model.

units.zh: 凡逋三調及衆責，在今年七月三十日前，悉同蠲除。
units.en: Every unpaid third impost and miscellaneous levy due before the thirtieth day of the seventh month of this year is forgiven in full.
units.literal: All overdue third imposts and assorted levies—everything before the thirtieth day of the seventh month of this year—is wholly remitted.

units.zh: 其備償封籍貨鬻未售，亦皆還主。
units.en: Property sealed for forced sale or pawned but not yet sold shall be returned to its owners.
units.literal: Goods registered for compulsory repayment and pawned but unsold shall all be returned to the owners.

units.zh: 禦府諸署池田邸冶，興廢沿事，本施一時，於今無用者，詳所罷省。
units.en: Ponds, fields, lodges, and smelters in the palace offices, begun or abandoned as times changed and meant only for the moment—whatever serves no purpose now should be examined and cut back.
units.literal: Ponds, fields, lodges, and foundries in the various offices of the imperial household—started or dropped as occasion required and meant for a time—whatever is useless today shall be reviewed for abolition or reduction.

units.zh: 公宜權禁，一以還民，關市征賦，務從優減。」
units.en: What ought to be barred to the state should be wholly returned to the people; tolls at the passes and market taxes should be eased as far as possible."
units.literal: What the state ought to forbid, let all be returned to the people; market tolls and taxes shall be kept as light as may be."

units.zh: 丙戌，詔曰：「近北掠餘口，悉充軍實。
units.en: Day bingxu: an edict said: "Lately northerners seized in raids have all been pressed into the army rolls.
units.literal: Day bingxu: An edict said: "Recently captives taken in the north were all filled into military rolls.

units.zh: 刑故無小，罔或攸赦，撫辜興仁，事深睿範。
units.en: The law says that in punishment no guilt is too small to escape—but to comfort the injured and stir benevolence is the deeper pattern of sage rule.
